then.say: Another one up from the road. Sit, if your legs allow it. This is Wick's Rest, the last honest shrine this side of the Abbey.
Rest at it and your wounds close and your phial fills. The dead get up again too, I'm afraid. Nothing is free.
Warm. The Drip hasn't touched you at all. Hm.

else.say: Still warm? Good. Keep it that way.

do.say: The slow death. First cold fingers, then a shine on the skin, then you're a candle that walks. The Great Wick keeps it back.
The Guttering Abbey, up the Hill Stair. Penitents go there to give themselves to the flame. None come back down.
The Tollwarden keeps its gatehouse. He takes a toll from everyone who passes. What he takes, you'll see.
You tell her his last words: that Anselm kept the count.
Anselm. I haven't heard that name said aloud in twenty years.
He wasn't cruel, you know. He was the only one up there who looked at their faces. Somebody had to.
Go on, then. You have his key. Go and see what he counted.
She reads the first page. Then the second. Her hands stop shaking somewhere around the tenth.
Names and weights. He wrote down the weights.
I knew. Not this. But I knew enough, and I kept the shrine lit and I didn't ask, because the shrine was all these people had.
Keep it. Somebody has to carry it up to him, and it can't be me. Not yet.

menu.text: What is behind the locked gate?

do.say: The carters' road, down to the Tallow Works. The carts go through full and come back empty. The Tollwarden has the key.
I don't know. And I'd rather not guess out loud. Keep your gloves on around the Order.
